title: A Chased Kangaroo Runs Into Water, Then Waits for the Dog to Follow

scenes.text: A kangaroo chased by a dog runs straight for water.
It wades out to where it can still stand, turns around, and waits. The kangaroo has its feet on the bottom. The dog has to swim.
In 2023, a man walking along the Murray River in Australia saw how that ends: a kangaroo holding his dog below the surface.
He fought the kangaroo off and the dog survived. But the story started a debate: was it really trying to drown the dog?
Wildlife ecologists say it's defence. Kangaroos have lived alongside dingoes for thousands of years, and heading for water is one way they learned to survive an attack.
To a kangaroo, your dog is a dingo. And in the water, the hunted one has the advantage.

description:
A kangaroo chased by dogs or dingoes will often head for water, where it can stand while its pursuer has to swim.
In 2023 a man on the Murray River in north-west Victoria found a kangaroo holding his dog under the surface; he drove it off and the dog survived. Wildlife ecologist Euan Ritchie of Deakin University says kangaroos probably treat dogs as dingoes, predators they have lived with for thousands of years, and that this behaviour is one way they survive attacks.
Did you know kangaroos did this?
